title: Score a table football goal from your three-man rod without spinning the rod
instruction: The ball is at your centre forward's feet. Shoot it into the goal on your right with your three-man rod, without spinning the rod.
context: Table football (foosball) is played in bars, offices, student unions and homes: you slide and turn a rod by its handle, and the little players fixed on it kick the ball. A shot from the three-man rod means sliding a forward in line with the ball, finding the gap past the opposing defence and goalie, and striking with a short, quick turn of the handle; spinning the rod (turning it more than a full turn) is against the rules, and so is putting a hand into the playfield.
setup: Station table; x forward from the line through the arm bases, y to the robot's left of their midpoint (bases at y +/-30.5 cm), heights from the table top. (1) A Best Choice Products 40 in tabletop foosball table (wooden cabinet 1016 mm long along y, 572 mm deep along x, 152 mm tall, about 10.7 kg; green playfield 30 mm up; a goal mouth 130 mm wide and 45 mm tall in the middle of each end wall, a catch box behind it), standing with its long side toward the robot, its near side at x 20.0 cm, centred on y 0. Eight 1/2 in chrome rods cross the playfield along x, 127 mm apart, their axes 72 mm above it; moulded players (22 mm thick, a 26 x 24 mm foot whose sole is 6 mm above the playfield) are fixed on them. From the left end: the robot's goalie (1), the robot's defence (2), the opponent's forwards (3), the robot's midfield (5), the opponent's midfield (5), the robot's forwards (3, players 170 mm apart), the opponent's defence (2, 200 mm apart) and the opponent's goalie (1). The robot's rods are red with their 32 mm rubber handles 100 mm out from the near side; the opponent's are blue with handles on the far side. Every rod is held still by a stop with its players hanging straight down, except the robot's three-man forward rod (handle at y -19.05 cm), which turns freely and slides +/-60 mm between its bumpers, centred. (2) A 36 mm white plastic ball (17 g) resting on the playfield, its surface 15 mm in front of (toward -y of) the forward rod's foot faces and its centre 38 mm beyond the field's centre line (away from the robot): centre at x 52.4, y -23.6 cm, in the lane between the opponent goalie's foot and the right-hand goal post. Both grippers open at the ready pose.
scoring: Goal: the ball wholly past the right-hand goal line inside the goal mouth (latched). On target: the ball reached the right-hand end wall within 100 mm of the goal mouth (latched). Progress: how far the ball travelled toward the right-hand goal. Spin: the forward rod turned more than 360 degrees one way from its start at any moment. Hand in the game: a gripper over the playfield below the cabinet's top, or within 5 mm of the ball, at any moment. Own goal: the ball past the left-hand goal line. 1.0: a goal, and both grippers 30 mm or more from the forward rod's handle for the last 1 s. 0.75: a goal, the handle still held. 0.5: on target without a goal. 0.25: the ball moved 150 mm or more toward the right-hand goal. 0: anything else, and the whole run on any spin, hand in the game or own goal. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. Real trial: the ball in the goal's catch box; the end-wall marks 100 mm either side of the mouth; a tape mark 150 mm toward the goal; the rod's turns and the hands from the trial video.
reset_notes: Ball back on its mark; the forward rod slid to centre with its players hanging straight down; every other rod in its stop. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rods, players and ball are rigid; the forward rod slides on a joint with 3 N of bushing friction and turns freely about it. Table size from the maker; the rods' positions and spacing, the players' shape, the goal mouth, the ball and the frictions are estimates. The playfield and rods are plain colours, with no printed graphics.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (600 steps, the run limit); demo: 1.0 (scripted, success at step 273)
